title: Unify benchmark host profiles and CI gating for tokens/sec & p95 regression detection
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description:
Problem: Our token throughput and latency benchmarks vary unpredictably across CI runs because host environments (driver, CUDA, base images, runner setup) are not standardized and test metadata is inconsistently recorded. This makes automated regression detection noisy and blocks safe rollouts.

Goal: Define a small set of canonical "host profiles" (driver + CUDA + pinned image + runner config), update the benchmark harness to emit standardized metadata (tokens/sec, p95, p99, sample counts, observer labels), and add CI-level regression detection that compares recent runs to a stable baseline with statistical checks and alerting.

Scope:
- Define 3 host profiles: play (dev), stable (production-like), and experimental (new drivers/quantization testing). Each profile will specify NVIDIA driver version, CUDA toolkit, pinned runtime image tag, and runner type.
- Standardize the benchmark harness to attach metadata labels: profile, driver_version, cuda_version, image_tag, runner_type, model_variant, sequence_length_distribution_id.
- Persist raw run artifacts (JSON) to the benchmark archive and export time-series metrics to the Grafana Prometheus namespace with stable metric names (bench_tokens_per_sec, bench_latency_p95_ms, bench_samples).
- Implement a regression detector job in CI: compare latest run window (N=5) to baseline (rolling median of previous 20 stable runs) using bootstrap CI and flag >5% tokens/sec drop or >10% p95 increase with p<0.05.
- Add blocking CI gate for PRs that touch runtime or serving code if the regression detector flags a failure for the stable profile.

Acceptance criteria:
- Three host profiles documented and pinned images published to container registry.
- Benchmark harness emits labelled JSON and Prometheus metrics for all profiles.
- Regression detector job runs in CI and produces human-readable failure reasons and links to artifacts.
- At least two non-trivial PRs tested in the new flow without false positives for one week.

Out-of-scope: Full rollout to Dedicated customer fleets, per-customer tuning, or automated rollback (handled by separate rollout automation work).
comments: 2025-02-10 Marcus Nguyen: Initial ticket created after noisy CI runs during runtime-1.19 smoke tests. Attached a short sample of JSON run artifacts to confluence.

2025-02-11 Aisha Patel: Proposed host profiles (dev=driver-525/cuda-11.8/pinned:ubuntu22.04-py3.10-cu11.8, stable=driver-535/cuda-12.1/pinned:ubuntu22.04-py3.11-cu12.1, experimental=driver-535/cuda-12.2-rc/pinned:ubuntu24.04-py3.11-cu12.2-rc) — needs ops sign-off.
2025-02-12 Oliver Chen (Infra): Confirmed registry tags and availability on k8s node pools; asked for migration plan for legacy runners.
2025-02-13 QA: Ran smoke harness across stable profile; observed baseline tokens/sec jitter ~2% and p95 variance ~4% (acceptable). Added additional warm-up iterations to harness.
2025-02-14 Marcus Nguyen: Implemented metric labels and exported bench_tokens_per_sec and bench_latency_p95_ms to Prometheus; PR #432 opened (link in attachments).

2025-02-15 Aisha Patel: Added CI regression detector recipe (bootstrap test) and configured it as optional gate on experimental and dev profiles; plan to flip stable profile gate to blocking after 72h of green runs.
migration_plan: 1) Publish pinned images and node pool labels. 2) Run benchmark harness on stable profile for 48h to build baseline. 3) Enable detector in CI as non-blocking. 4) Observe for 72h; if <1% false-positive rate, promote to blocking gate. 5) Document rollback steps and allow opt-out per PR via experimental label.
risks: Pinned image drift (registry tag mutated), driver incompatibilities with older kernels, increased CI time. Mitigations: immutability policy for tags, automated smoke on baremetal runners, and test time budget in CI.
rolling_back: If the regression detector causes spurious failures, revert the CI job to non-blocking and investigate run artifacts. Keep a safety flag in CI to bypass gating for emergency fixes.
notes: Design decisions: use bootstrap rather than t-test because metric distributions are non-normal; record raw samples to allow post-hoc analysis. Include sequence_length_distribution_id so we can group runs by realistic prompt mixes. Metrics should be tagged with model_variant (float16/quantized) so comparisons are apples-to-apples.
qa_plan: Run 3 canonical models (small/medium/large) across the stable profile with 50 runs each, collect tokens/sec and p95, validate detector false-positive rate under 72-hour window.
